insuranceNote.title: COMESA Yellow Card vs border insurance
insuranceNote.body: The Yellow Card is compulsory third-party liability across COMESA member states (Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Tanzania, and others). Buy before the queue from your insurer or AA South Africa. South Africa and Mozambique are not COMESA members but motorists leaving those countries can obtain a Yellow Card under a Business-to-Business arrangement. Border-issued insurance is sometimes available but queues and premiums are unpredictable — budget extra time and cash if you rely on it.

countries.name: South Africa

fees.notes: Ensure rental cross-border letter covers return

fees.amount: Included in SA policy or rental
fees.notes: Yellow Card needed when leaving SA into COMESA states
Gauteng e-tag speeds up N1/N3/N12/N17

countries.tip: Unabridged birth certificate for travelling minors. ZA sticker on rear of foreign-registered vehicles entering SA.

countries.name: Namibia

fees.notes: Paid at land borders; temporary import permit stamped
Or valid Yellow Card if driving onward to COMESA
Passport stamp + vehicle declaration

countries.tip: NAD pegged 1:1 to rand — cards work in towns; carry cash at remote posts.

countries.name: Botswana

fees.notes: National road safety levy may apply

fees.amount: Yellow Card or P150–250 at border
fees.notes: Police checks expect proof of cover
Vehicle registration + passport required

countries.tip: Strict vet controls — no fresh meat or dairy. Declare camping food; tinned goods usually OK.

countries.name: Zambia

fees.notes: Road Transport and Safety Agency levy at borders
Often bundled with road fees — keep receipt
Border purchase possible but slow; COMESA preferred
Separate from KAZA UniVisa (per person, not per vehicle)

countries.tip: KAZA UniVisa USD 50 is per traveller for ZM↔ZW circuits — not a vehicle fee.

countries.name: Zimbabwe

fees.notes: Zimbabwe National Road Administration — pay at border
Often collected with ZINARA; exact USD notes preferred

fees.amount: USD 20–40 at border or Yellow Card
fees.notes: Beitbridge queues longest if buying insurance on arrival
Bridge tolls at Victoria Falls / Kazungula are separate small fees

countries.tip: Carry clean USD small notes — torn or old bills refused at many desks.

countries.name: Mozambique

fees.notes: Vehicle declaration + passport
Mandatory — obtain before queue when possible
Lebombo/Ressano Garcia busiest from Kruger

countries.tip: e-Visa or visa-on-arrival for most tourists — separate from vehicle fees.

countries.name: Malawi

fees.notes: Paid at land borders
Border purchase available at Mchinji and Songwe
Fuel availability can be limited — plan ahead

countries.tip: COMESA Yellow Card is the fastest option on multi-country loops via Zambia.

countries.name: Lesotho

fees.notes: Maseru Bridge, Caledonspoort, Ficksburg, Sani Pass

fees.amount: SA rental cover if letter permits Lesotho
fees.notes: Confirm on cross-border letter before departure
Sani Pass: 4×4 mandatory; controls at summit

countries.tip: Single-entry SA visa holders: entering Lesotho exits South Africa — you need multi-entry SA visa to return.

countries.name: Eswatini

fees.notes: Oshoek/Ngwenya and Golela/Lavumisa main tourist posts
Lilangeni pegged 1:1 to rand
Often faster than busier SA-only posts

countries.tip: Same SA visa trap as Lesotho — plan multi-entry if looping Kingdom Circuit from Kruger.
